حَائِكٌ : see art. حوك. [In the present day, ↓ حَيَّاكٌ signifies the same; i. e. A weaver.] ＝
-A2- Also, and ↓ حَيَّاكٌ , applied to a man; and ↓ حَيَّاكَةٌ and ↓ حَيْكَانَةٌ and ↓ حِيكَانَةٌ and ↓ حُيَكَانَةٌ , (K, TA,) and, accord. to the K, ↓ حَيَكَى , but this is an inf. n., and is here a mistake for ↓ حِيكَى , originally حُيْكَى, mentioned by Sb, (TA,) applied to a woman; Walking, or who walks, in the manner denoted by the verb حاك, i. e., with an elegant and a proud and self-conceited gait, &c. (K, TA.) ＝
-A3- And the first, i. e. حائك, Becoming fixed in the heart, and disquieting one. (Az, TA in art. حوك.) [See 1.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
